article.body_html:
Keeping the same bike for several months is a different proposition from renting for a weekend, and it is fair to ask whether the terms can reflect that. The mistake is to treat the conversation as a contest over the price. A shop that rents bikes by the month may plan around each bike's availability, upkeep and return, so a long-stay renter has something to offer besides money: certainty. This guide sets out what you might ask for, what you might offer in return and how to raise it politely. Whether Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà would agree to any of it, you will only learn by asking.

Start with the shop's own starting point

The shop gives reference prices for a month of 1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND for a manual bike and 1,200,000 to 2,000,000 VND for an automatic bike. Those are ranges, so first ask which figure applies to the bike you want and what it includes. A request for better terms only makes sense once you know what the base rate covers. The reference prices are not offers, so the figure that applies to you is whatever the shop confirms in writing for your booking.

What you might ask for

  • A fixed rate for the whole period, so that the figure does not change in the third month.
  • A lower monthly rate in return for a longer commitment. The shop may or may not offer one.
  • The same bike, or the same type of bike, throughout, if you have settled on a model that suits you.
  • Service on a schedule, with the shop saying who arranges it, who pays and what happens to your use of the bike while it is done.
  • A replacement plan for the case where the bike has to be withdrawn for repair.

What a shop might reasonably ask in return

A request is more credible when it comes with something the shop values. Think about which of these you could honestly offer, and offer only what you will do.

You could offerWhy a shop might value itMake sure you can keep it
A fixed period, such as three months, agreed at the startThe shop can plan around a bike that stays rentedCheck your own plans, and ask what happens if you need to leave sooner
Payment on an agreed schedule, made on timeThe shop knows when money arrivesMatch the schedule to your income
Keeping the same bike throughoutThe bike's wear and condition are easy to follow from one month to the nextBe sure the bike suits you for the whole period; how to choose the right bike helps
Returning the bike on the agreed date and in the recorded conditionThe bike is ready for the next renterPhotograph the bike at handover and again at return
Telling the shop early about changesThe shop can adjust its plans tooAgree how you will tell it: a message, a call or both

How to raise it politely

Ask a question; do not make a demand. A message along these lines keeps the tone friendly and gives the shop something specific to answer:

Hello, I would like to rent a manual bike from the start date for about three months, and I can pay on a regular schedule. If I commit to the whole period, is there anything the shop could change in the monthly rate or the terms? If not, I would still like to know exactly what the rate includes.

If you have a quote from another shop, it is fair to mention it as long as you compare like with like: the same type of bike, the same period and the same inclusions. Comparing two quotes line by line shows how.

What to avoid

  • Do not press after a clear no. A posted price is the shop's decision.
  • Do not promise a period you may not keep. A commitment you cannot honour costs you more than a discount saves.
  • Do not trade away the checks. Skipping your own walk-around or handover photos is not a concession to the shop; it only removes your own protection.
  • Do not leave anything agreed only by voice. Anything the shop accepts, whether a rate, a period, a bike or a service, belongs in the written record.

Put what is agreed in writing

When the shop says yes to something, repeat it back in a message: the bike, the dates, the rate, any service arrangements and what happens if either side needs to end the rental early. Keep that message with your booking record. For the shop's own monthly rates, see its page on monthly rental in Hanoi; to raise terms, message or call 0334 699 969 during opening hours, 09:00 to 21:00.
